concepts.title: Congruent Figures
concepts.definition: Figures that areput differently,  exact copies of each other or have the same shape and size are said to be congruent. Congruent figures can be superimposed exactly, one over the other.
concepts.key_idea: Two figures are congruent if they fit exactly over each other, possibly after rotation or flipping.

concepts.title: SSS Congruence Condition

concepts.title: Congruence Notation and Correspondence
concepts.definition: When two triangles are congruent, there are corresponding vertices, sides and angles which fit exactly over each other. The notation ΔABC ≅ ΔXYZ implies A corresponds to X, B to Y, and C to Z.
concepts.key_idea: The order of vertices in the congruence statement must reflect the physical correspondence.

concepts.title: RHS Congruence Condition
concepts.definition: When a side and a hypotenuse of a right-angled triangle are equal to a side and the hypotenuse of another right-angled triangle, they are congruent.
concepts.key_idea: Special case for right triangles involving the hypotenuse and one other side.
